provider) for this CLI's actual business logic.

commands.name: status
commands.description:
Report every provider's credential: where it comes from and whether it works. Never prints values.

Without --check only presence is reported (status `unchecked` or `missing`).
Exits 0 when every required provider is ok/unchecked (an optional one may be
missing), 3 when any required provider has a problem or any credential is
invalid/expired, 2 on a usage error. A per-target provider (one credential per
site/host/account) gets one entry per stored target, named `<kind>:<target>`. The --json shape is a cross-tool contract:
`tool`, `version`, `checked_at`, `credentials[]` with `provider`, `required`,
`fields`, `source`, `source_ref`, `status`, `expires_at`, `quota`, `message`.

Example: semkit auth status --check --json

commands.name: read
commands.description:
Read a table, run the steps in the order written, write the result: one pipeline.

Each step works on the current table. A change step rewrites the working column
(with --as NAME it writes a new column), a filter keeps or drops rows, a report
(n-grams) makes its table the current one and its first text column the working one.
After each step one line goes to stderr: the step, the rows before and after it,
the cells it changed. Every step and option is checked before the input is read.

Every column is read as text; an empty cell is an empty string. An option that
takes items takes a comma list 'a,b', @FILE (one item per line) or @NAME of a list
(@stopwords, the marker lists). `semkit read IN STEP --help` shows a step.

Example: semkit read core.csv remove-words --items купить dupes --kind lemmas --action drop write out.csv

options.name: --column
options.description: The working column the steps read and change; by default the first text column.

options.name: --whole
options.description: Read a text file as one cell of the column text (an article).

options.name: --trace
options.description: Write every cell a step changes and every row it drops to FILE as JSONL: row, step, column, before, after.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON output.

options.name: --quiet

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Read and run every step, print the summary, write nothing.

commands.name: ngrams
commands.description:
Every run of `n` words over all phrases, counted: a table ngram, count, docs, sum and forms.

count: occurrences. docs: in how many distinct index values (texts, when `sk.split_text` cut the phrases) the gram occurs at least once; the add-in has no such column, it is a semkit addition, so the conformance cases compare count and sum only. sum: with `weight`. forms: with `lemmas`, the word forms met for the gram, most frequent first, joined by ', ' («диваны, диван»); for a gram of several words its distinct spellings, at most 5.

Sorted by count, biggest first, then by ngram. Words are compared by case and ё.
lemmas: count lemmas of the words («диваны» is «диван»), by `lemmatizer`.
stopwords: False makes the runs of words that are no stopwords; a stopword between two of them stays inside the gram («купить диван в москве» gives «купить диван» and «диван в москве»), as «Биграмм без учета стоп-слов»; stopwords are found in any case (ADR 0005).
weight: a numeric column of the table; `sum` adds its value once per occurrence.

The step counts the working column; the table replaces the current one, its column ngram is the working one.

Example: semkit read core.csv ngrams write out.csv

options.description: See the description above.

options.name: --lemmas

commands.name: dupes
commands.description:
Duplicates by `kind`: exact, explicit (case, ё→е, spaces), implicit (other word order) or lemmas.

`action`: mark_except_first (a bool, the first of a group is False), mark_all (every member of a group of 2+), drop (keep the first, drop the rest). With `against` a phrase is a duplicate when its key is in that Series.

The step marks the duplicates of the working column in a new column <column>_dupes; with --action drop it keeps only the first row of each group.

Example: semkit read core.csv dupes --kind exact --action mark_except_first write out.csv

commands.name: find-words
commands.description:
Whole words of a phrase equal to `items`, compared by case and ё (`norm_phrase`).

mode: "any" — any of the words; "all" — only phrases holding every one of them.
where: "anywhere", "start" (the first word only) or "end" (the last word only).
ignore_punct: punctuation at the edges of a word does not count («диван,» is «диван»).
lemmatizer: compare lemmas («диваны» is «диван»); None compares the words as they are.

find-words marks the rows where the matcher finds something, in a new column <column>_find of true and false.

Example: semkit read core.csv find-words --items купить write out.csv

commands.name: find-phrases
commands.description:
Phrases of a list, found as whole words («угловой диван» is not in «угловойдиван» or «угловой диван,»).

Words compare in any case, ё as е; punctuation glued to a word counts. find, remove and extract take the same phrases, as `sk.markers(user=...)` does: left to right, for each word the longest phrase that starts there (in words, then in characters; a tie keeps the list order), and the words of a taken phrase start no other. remove keeps the case of the other words; extract gives the phrases as the list spells them, joined by ', '.

find-phrases marks the rows where the matcher finds something, in a new column <column>_find of true and false.

Example: semkit read core.csv find-phrases --items купить write out.csv

commands.name: find-chars
commands.description:
The characters of one type.

kind: "latin" (A-Z a-z), "cyrillic" (А..ӿ and Ё: not the capitals Є І Ї), "digits" (0-9), "letters_digits" (letters that have a case, and 0-9), "punctuation" (every other character but whitespace: also «-», «№» and letters without a case), "upper" (upper-case letters), "ua" (the Ukrainian letters і ї є ґ). remove cuts the characters out; a punctuation character leaves a space («Диван-кровать» → «Диван кровать»). extract keeps latin, cyrillic and digits with the whitespace between them («120x200» → «120200»); for the other kinds it gives the runs joined by a space.

find-chars marks the rows where the matcher finds something, in a new column <column>_find of true and false.

Example: semkit read core.csv find-chars --kind latin write out.csv
